function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here are some common ways to order a cake, depending on what you’re looking for:

| Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips |
|--------|----------------|--------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, custom‑made cakes, often with seasonal flavors | Call or visit the bakery’s website; many accept online orders via their own site or platforms like **Etsy** or **Shopify** | Ask about delivery times, special dietary needs (gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free), and whether they can accommodate custom designs. |
| **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide or regional delivery, often with a wide variety of styles | Websites such as **Goldbelly**, **Cake Delivery**, **Baker’s Dozen**, or **Bakery.com** let you browse, customize, and pay online. | Check delivery windows, shipping fees, and read reviews. Some services offer “same‑day” delivery in major cities. |
| **Grocery stores & supermarkets** | Ready‑made cakes, often with a “pick‑up” or “delivery” option | Many chains (Walmart, Kroger, Safeway, Tesco, etc.) have online ordering for bakery items. | Look for “express” or “same‑day” pickup options. Some stores partner with delivery apps (Instacart, Shipt). |
| **Specialty dessert shops** | Artisan cakes, often with unique flavors or themes | Search for local specialty shops (e.g., “artisan chocolate cake shop”) and check if they offer online ordering or phone orders. | Great for themed parties or gourmet flavors. |
| **Meal‑delivery & subscription services** | Cakes delivered as part of a meal kit or dessert subscription | Services like **HelloFresh**, **Blue Apron**, or **Dessert Club** sometimes include cake options. | Good if you want a recurring cake delivery or a cake that pairs with a meal. |
| **DIY kits** | All the ingredients and instructions to bake at home | Sites like **Amazon**, **Etsy**, or specialty baking sites sell cake kits. | Fun for a personal touch or if you enjoy baking. |

### Quick Steps to Order

1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc.) and any dietary restrictions.
2. **Choose a style** (classic vanilla, chocolate, red velvet, custom design, etc.).
3. **Pick a vendor** from the table above that fits your location and budget.
4. **Place the order**: either online or by phone. Provide delivery address, preferred delivery time, and any special instructions.
5. **Confirm details**: double‑check the order summary, delivery fee, and estimated arrival time.
6. **Pay**: most sites accept credit cards, PayPal, or Apple Pay. Some local bakeries may accept cash on delivery.

### If You’re in a Specific City

If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated bakeries or delivery services in your area. Just drop the location, and I’ll fetch the latest info for you!
